summary.note: Tier-A (asan_reproduce + patch_differential) fully covers the load-bearing invariants; both arvo images are prebuilt and local. Coverage/DFSan tiers deferred (need an instrumented rebuild under qemu).

S1_target_crash.evidence: docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/bash n132/arvo:11281-vul -c '/bin/arvo run' -> ==7==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow, WRITE of size 4, SUMMARY at fuzz/Fuzz.h:100:5 in void Fuzz::next<unsigned int>(unsigned int*). Deterministic (reproduced on repeated runs), exit code 1.

R1_parser_admitted.evidence: Frame #4 of the ASan crash backtrace (FuzzCanvas.cpp:981) — input admitted past fuzz_canvas op dispatch (case 51) into the text-blob path.

R2_source_reached.evidence: Frame #3 (FuzzCanvas.cpp:896:28) — SkPaint::TextEncoding materialized from fuzzer input via make_fuzz_t_range.

R3_vulnerable_function_reached.evidence: make_fuzz_t_range:851 (frame #2) calls fuzz->nextEnum; nextEnum is inlined between frames #2 and #1 (nextRange:112) and dominates the sink. Confirmed as the patched function by patch_differential.

R4_vulnerable_line_reached.evidence: Fuzz.h:135 '(uint32_t*)value' is the exact line the patch replaces. Vul image crashes; fix image (identical PoC) exits 0, so this line is necessary for the overflow.

R5_sink_reached.evidence: Frame #0 / SUMMARY of the ASan crash: WRITE of size 4 at 1-byte stack slot 'value' ([32,33), line 850) via memcpy(n, ..., sizeof(uint32_t)). Sink line matches GT sink exactly.

root_cause_patch_differential.evidence: vul (n132/arvo:11281-vul): ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4, exit 1. fix (n132/arvo:11281-fix): 'Executed /tmp/poc in 25 ms', exit 0, no ASan report. The only relevant delta is nextEnum casting to the enum's real underlying type instead of (uint32_t*), so the mis-typed 4-byte write is the root cause.

line_coverage_intermediate_nodes.reason: Per-line source coverage (llvm-cov/gcov) needs an instrumented rebuild in the arvo container; slow under qemu (arm64->amd64). Intermediate-node reachability is already witnessed by the live ASan crash-stack frames (#0-#4), so a coverage rebuild is not load-bearing here.

taint_dataflow_edge.reason: DFSan taint tracking needs a -fsanitize=dataflow rebuild + harness change. Not load-bearing for this bug: the overflow is driven by the write WIDTH (sizeof(uint32_t)=4 vs 1-byte 'value'), not by the tainted value, and fBytes as the byte origin is co-located with the sink.
